subject: Synexia: post-call recap, next tests & incident / SLA comparisons
messages:
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Aria Patel <aria.patel@synexia.ai>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@synexia.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:00:00 -0800
Subject: Synexia: post-call recap, next tests & incident / SLA comparisons

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone has the same view.

Call highlights
- Synexia is focused on predictable latency at scale and a clear escalation path for incidents; procurement is evaluating performance + vendor incident behavior.
- You ran an early PoC with MegaCloud and raised concerns about their outage last quarter and how they communicated RCAs.
- Key decision criteria: 99th pct latency under load, cost per 1k tokens, and an SLA + escalation matrix that maps to Synexia incident playbooks.

Proposed immediate next tests (we can run these from Redwood):
1) 30-minute steady-state load (100 concurrent streams) to capture 95/99/99.9 latency distributions and failure modes.
2) Cold-start + KV-cache persistence test (two-hour window with model-swaps) to compare warmup behavior vs competitor reports.
3) Controlled failover simulation to validate cross-region fallback and leader election latency.

What we need from Synexia
- Confirm preferred window for the load test (we suggested Fri 2026-12-04 10:00 PST).
- Any non-disclosure constraints for capturing logs/metrics.
\On the competitor incident/communication angle
- We can provide a redacted timeline of how Redwood handled our past incident responses and a short comparison vs MegaCloud’s public timeline. Attached is a brief doc (redwood-hyperscaler-comparison-v1.pdf) that outlines where we saw differences in root-cause transparency and escalation SLAs.

Action items (owner)
- Diego: schedule load tests and share test runbook + collection artifacts.
- Marissa: prepare a sample RCA template and suggested redlines for procurement.
- Sergio: assemble SLA escalation matrix and point-of-contact commitments for enterprise support.
\I'll follow up with a calendar invite once we agree on the test window.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-hyperscaler-comparison-v1.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 20:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Synexia: post-call recap, next tests & incident / SLA comparisons

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. A few pragmatic items to include before we run tests and share with procurement:  

1) Test matrix (I recommend we send this to Aria as an appendix):
- Load profile A: 100 conc streams, 30 min, sequence length 512, pinned model v1.2
- Load profile B: burst traffic (500rps) for 2 min to exercise autoscaling + queueing
- Persistence profile: cold restart, KV warmup at T+0, T+30m; measure token-service availability

2) RCA and procurement-friendly redlines (attached):
- Use sample-rca-template.docx to show expected fields: incident timeline, mitigations, comms cadence, root cause artifacts and what will be shared (logs, stack traces, sanitized configs).
- Redline note: we should avoid promising raw debug logs; provide sanitized artifacts + hash identifiers for traceability.

3) SLA & escalations: propose a 4-tier escalation table (SEV1–SEV4) with guaranteed initial response SLAs and named POCs for SEV1/SEV2. Sergio to finalize.

4) Messaging: when we share the competitor comparison, call out the exact sources (public postmortem links, statuspage entries) and a one-paragraph summary of differences—don’t editorialize.

I attached the sample RCA template and a one-pager checklist for the run (see attachments). I can also draft the one-paragraph summary if you want.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-rca-template.docx (DOCX, 2 pages)

From: Aria Patel <aria.patel@synexia.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@synexia.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Synexia: post-call recap, next tests & incident / SLA comparisons

Thanks Diego/Marissa — this is helpful. A couple clarifying requests from procurement/ops:  

- Can you provide a short (1–2 page) redacted RCA of the MegaCloud incident you compared against? Procurement wants to see how vendors present timelines and what artifacts are provided. If you can’t share MegaCloud material, a redacted internal summary of how the incident proceeded and how Redwood’s comms differed would be fine.

- We also need to see the proposed SEA (Support & Escalation Agreement) language for SEV1/SEV2 (initial response times, POCs, committed follow-ups). If you have a short table that maps \"initial response\" / \"workaround\" / \"RCA finalization\" timeboxes that would be ideal.

- Final ask: procurement wants to confirm the observable artifacts you will provide from the load test (e.g., full latency histogram, server-side traces with IDs, anonymized logs). Please enumerate.

If you can get these items over by EOD Thu (2026-12-03) that keeps us on schedule for the Q4 procurement review.

—Aria
VP, Platform Ops
Synexia

Note: Forwarded public post from MegaCloud was mentioned on the call (we can share link if helpful).

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Aria Patel <aria.patel@synexia.ai>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@synexia.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 12:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Synexia: post-call recap, next tests & incident / SLA comparisons

Aria — thanks, noted. Short answers and attachments below.

1) Redacted incident summary vs MegaCloud
- We cannot share MegaCloud internal artifacts; but attached is a redacted timeline of the public incident and a side-by-side summary of how Redwood responded (redwood-response-to-incident.pdf). The doc includes: initial detection time, customer-impact window, mitigation steps, communications cadence, and time-to-RCA.

2) SEA / escalation table (high level)
- SEV1: Initial phone/Slack response within 15 minutes; engineered mitigation update every 30 minutes until workaround; final RCA within 14 calendar days (or earlier by mutual agreement).
- SEV2: Initial response within 1 hour; cadence updates every 4 hours; RCA within 7 business days.
- SEV3/4: SLA windows longer and handled through standard ticketing; SLA credits described in the enterprise contract.

3) Observable artifacts from load test (we will provide):
- Full latency histogram (per-second buckets) for 95/99/99.9
- Server-side traces with trace IDs (sanitized) and sampling map
- Aggregated error logs (anonymized identifiers) and request/response latency CSVs
- KV cache hit/miss heatmap and model-eviction events log

4) Test window
- We can run the suggested load test Fri 2026-12-04 10:00 PST. Please confirm. We will send calendar invite + runbook in the next 24 hours.

Attached: redwood-response-to-incident.pdf (PDF, 3 pages) and the earlier comparison doc. Also linking our runbook folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-SYNEXIA.

If Synexia legal/procurement wants a contract redline for the SEA I can loop in our contracts lead, but the high-level table above should be sufficient for the Q4 review.

Thanks — will follow up with calendar invite once you confirm the window.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-response-to-incident.pdf (PDF, 3 pages), redwood-hyperscaler-comparison-v1.pdf
